raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Ming's DiT computes RMSNorm statistics in FP32 and rounds normalized values to BF16 before multiplying by the learned weight. Its native implementation launches separate square, mean, reciprocal-square-root, cast, and multiply operations throughout the denoising loop. This reuses the existing ordered RMSNorm implementation to reduce those launches while preserving the native result.

## Modifications

- Add `eps=1e-5` to the shared cast-before-weight operator, keeping its existing `1e-6` default and epilogues unchanged.
- Extend its ordered reduction to width 3840. Widths 128/3840 use the ordered path for eligible row counts; other shapes, including width 2560, retain ATen mean with fused pointwise operations.
- Dispatch `MingRMSNorm.forward_native` through the existing per-signature bit-exact gate. Residual, compile, unsupported dtype/epsilon, and noncontiguous input/weight cases retain native behavior.
- Add focused reduction-boundary, mixed-magnitude, model-dispatch, CUDA graph replay, and native compile fallback coverage. No new flags or model weights are introduced.

## Accuracy Tests

Baseline: `af21e2b989e482cfdce39689126562f2209d53ac`  
Final head: `c77f23077712f4f6e43654e6492079f649894284`  
Checkpoint: `inclusionAI/Ming-Image-0.1-Design@c57c49689d12ef7d4e24a170014f1dc43d3ce258`.

On B300, 59 norm/kernel tests and 37 Ming tests passed. Full native quality runs cover short/long T2I prompts, seeds 42/43/44, image editing, and repeated requests. Final and pre-cleanup outputs are byte-identical to the matching main topology, including all 216 warmup/formal benchmark PNGs. Both SP2 ranks execute the norm operator and verify its signatures; no gate was disabled.

High quality, CFG=2, native sequential two-output generation, and the lossless revisit all pass against the corresponding main outputs. All 44 compatibility PNGs retain the expected identities; all eight high-mode comparisons are also byte-identical to lossless (RGBA/RGB/alpha/black and white composites: SSIM=1, zero maximum error, infinite PSNR). The two-output case is sequential multioutput, not dynamic batch2.

**BCG limitation:** both main and final capture one graph per worker and replay it only during warmup (12 replays per worker). All six serving cases miss the warmed signature: 84 misses for single-GPU T2I and 168 across the two edit ranks, zero serving replays and zero serving captures. The final norm operator executes 205 times during each capture, so capture includes the new path, but these requests subsequently use eager fallback. T2I capture wall time is 0.586s main / 2.338s final; edit captures take 2.130–2.143s main / 2.960–2.961s final per rank. These instrumented first-capture costs include preparation and are not amortized performance claims. Full capture memory and request-state records are retained. No new BCG serving support or BCG speedup is claimed.

Actual main/final generated images are shown below; previews use identical resizing. The original RGBA PNGs, exact requests, and hashes are retained in the evidence archives.

![Ming native text-to-image: main and final](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-ming-norm-evidence-20261027/text-to-image.jpg)

![Ming native image editing: main and final](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-ming-norm-evidence-20261027/image-edit.jpg)

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Fixed physical B300 GPU pool 0/1; T2I uses GPU0, editing uses Ulysses2 on both. Native BF16 DiT/text/VAE with FP32 latents and CPU RNG, 1024×1024, 12 steps, guidance 1, seed 42, PNG compression 0, all components resident. These are repeated saved requests with the existing native conditioning cache warmed. They are not cold-prompt latency measurements.

Each scenario runs `[main, pre-cleanup, final, final, pre-cleanup, main]` twice: 12 fresh servers, 3 warmups and 6 measured requests per server, 24 formal samples per arm. The timer covers HTTP submission through receipt of all response bytes, including native image generation/saving/encoding; client decoding and evidence copies are excluded. Profiler and synchronized stage diagnostics run separately. Tested GPUs are checked for foreign processes at every boundary; unrelated work on GPUs 4–7 is recorded in the raw telemetry.

| Scenario | Main E2E p50 / p95 (s) | Final E2E p50 / p95 (s) | p50 reduction | Sequential req/s main → final | Denoise main → final (s) | Peak allocated GiB per GPU main → final |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| T2I · 1 GPU | 1.7494 / 1.7559 | 1.3861 / 1.3935 | 20.77% | 0.572 → 0.721 | 1.6845 → 1.3209 | 49.430 → 49.430 |
| Edit · SP2 | 1.4558 / 1.4687 | 1.1166 / 1.1290 | 23.30% | 0.687 → 0.895 | 1.2459 → 0.9077 | 32.934 → 32.934 |

Denoise values are medians from separate synchronized diagnostics, using the slower rank for SP2. The empirical p95 uses 24 formal requests per arm. The workload has concurrency 1. Startup, warmup requests, reserved memory, and every individual sample remain in the raw results.

The full native T2I profile drops from 31,783 CUDA kernels on main to 14,587 at the final head. The identical profile output PNG is verified. This profile establishes the launch reduction; its instrumented duration is not used as an E2E benchmark.

**Baseline selection.** Both native TP2 and SP2 T2I alternatives fail the predeclared image-quality thresholds and remain recorded as failed cells. For editing, both pass; two main A/A medians are 1.7801/1.7824s for TP2 and 1.4499/1.4564s for SP2, versus 2.3420/2.3396s for single GPU. The final edit comparison therefore uses SP2.

**Cleanup retest.** Pre-cleanup `e94a5034a8d3b4ff1f607911aca1d8342ff79c95` is measured alongside the final head in the same symmetric runs. Cleanup removes redundant optional-argument guards and simplifies tests. All changed files were reviewed and pinned pre-commit checks pass.

| Scenario | Final vs main reduction, rounds 1 / 2 | Final vs pre-cleanup latency change, rounds 1 / 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| T2I | 20.64% / 20.89% | +0.134% / -0.004% |
| Edit · SP2 | 23.06% / 23.49% | -0.500% / -0.418% |

Initial single-GPU T2I A/A median drift is 0.099% for main and 0.376% for pre-cleanup; selected main SP2 edit A/A drift is 0.447%. Adjacent final pairs in the formal run drift by 0.237%/0.289% for T2I and 0.199%/0.153% for editing. The largest positive round cleanup change is +0.134% (T2I), below the measured noise; both edit rounds improve. Pooled mean/p95 cleanup changes are +0.093%/−0.036% for T2I and −0.459%/−0.708% for edit. The retest detects no performance regression from cleanup; these small differences are not claimed as a separate optimization or a population-tail guarantee.

**vLLM-Omni comparison.** Frozen native Omni `817d4c17feb702289a2d2b2cbacfd594c262b7a7` uses the same checkpoint, prompts, inputs, seeds, shape, steps, guidance, and two-GPU budget through its complete VLM→connector→DiT→RGBA pipeline. Its default FlashInfer MoE path fails same-input repeatability. Native Triton MoE restores repeatability, and native regional dynamic compilation with precision-cast emulation is confirmed to execute. Both still fail the quality gate for all 7 T2I samples and 2 of 4 edit samples against the selected SGLang references; edit seeds 43/44 have RGB SSIM around 0.936–0.939, below 0.95. No Omni speedup is claimed, and these cells are not counted as quality-qualified cross-framework performance results. All attempts and images are retained.

**Scope.** This validates Ming-Image-0.1-Design on B300, with the documented native configurations. The separately trained Layer checkpoint and other GPU architectures are not benchmarked here. Existing BCG compatibility findings are reported above; this PR does not claim new BCG coverage. The default kernel epsilon remains compatible with existing MOSS call sites.

**Reproduction and raw evidence:** [release assets](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/tag/b300-ming-norm-evidence-20261027). The package contains fixed source SHAs and patches, commands/environments, request fixtures, every timing/quality result, traces, failed alternatives, archive manifests/checksums, and actual media provenance. Reproduce the commands in the archive on idle GPUs; do not run the profiler during the HTTP benchmark.

## Checklist

- [x] Scoped pre-commit formatting and style checks.
- [x] Focused unit/kernel tests and real native model validation.
- [x] Accuracy, saved-request speed, cleanup retest, and profile evidence.
- [x] No new user-facing flags; behavior and limitations documented here.
- [ ] Upstream GPU CI/reviewer approval (Draft).

@BBuf AMD CI jobs started failing after this PR was merged, and #47118 proposes a fix. Could you review it?

test_ming_image.py::test_ming_norm_fusion_replay_and_native_fallback, added by this PR, is skipped only when torch.cuda.is_available() is false, which is never the case on ROCm, and it asserts that the fused RMSNorm kernel runs once. can_use_rmsnorm_cast_before_weight requires is_cuda(), so ROCm takes the native path and the test fails with call_count 0 on rocm10 and rocm724.

files.patch:
@@ -1,7 +1,7 @@
 # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-"""MOSSImage RMSNorm: FP32 statistics, BF16 rounding before learned scale.
+"""RMSNorm with FP32 statistics and BF16 rounding before learned scale.
 
-For widths 128/3072 with at least 16 rows, reproduce ATen's vectorized FP32
+For widths 128/3072/3840 with at least 16 rows, reproduce ATen's vectorized FP32
 mean reduction in one kernel. CUDA Reduce.cuh uses 32 lanes, four accumulators
 per lane, sequential fragment accumulation, then descending shuffle offsets.
 Other shapes retain ATen's mean with fused pointwise operations around it.
@@ -32,6 +32,7 @@ def _ordered_rstd(
     ROWS: tl.constexpr,
     HEADS: tl.constexpr = 1,
     TOKEN_STRIDE: tl.constexpr = 0,
+    EPS: tl.constexpr = 1e-6,
 ):
     rows = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * ROWS + tl.arange(0, ROWS)
     if TOKEN_STRIDE == 0 or TOKEN_STRIDE == HEADS * DIM:
@@ -59,7 +60,7 @@ def _ordered_rstd(
     total = _fold_halves(total, ROWS, 2)
     total = _fold_halves(total, ROWS, 1)
     mean = mul_rn_f32(tl.reshape(total, (ROWS,)), 1.0 / DIM)
-    return cuda_rsqrtf(mean + 1e-6)
+    return cuda_rsqrtf(mean + EPS)
 
 
 @triton.jit
@@ -71,9 +72,10 @@ def _ordered_norm_kernel(
     DIM: tl.constexpr,
     ROWS: tl.constexpr,
     BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    EPS: tl.constexpr,
 ):
     rows = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * ROWS + tl.arange(0, ROWS)
-    rstd = _ordered_rstd(X, M, DIM, ROWS)
+    rstd = _ordered_rstd(X, M, DIM, ROWS, EPS=EPS)
 
     cols = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
     mask = (rows[:, None] < M) & (cols[None, :] < DIM)
@@ -163,15 +165,22 @@ def _square_kernel(X, Squared, N: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
 
 @triton.jit
 def _normalize_kernel(
-    X, Mean, Weight, Out, N: tl.constexpr, DIM: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr
+    X,
+    Mean,
+    Weight,
+    Out,
+    N: tl.constexpr,
+    DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    EPS: tl.constexpr,
 ):
     offsets = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
     mask = offsets < N
     x = tl.load(X + offsets, mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
     mean = tl.load(Mean + offsets // DIM, mask, 0)
     weight = tl.load(Weight + offsets % DIM, mask, 0).to(tl.float32)
-    normalized = mul_rn_f32(x, cuda_rsqrtf(mean + 1e-6))
-    # This rounding precedes gamma in MOSSImage, unlike conventional RMSNorm.
+    normalized = mul_rn_f32(x, cuda_rsqrtf(mean + EPS))
+    # Round before gamma, as required by MOSSImage and Ming-Image.
     normalized = normalized.to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
     tl.store(Out + offsets, mul_rn_f32(normalized, weight), mask)
 
@@ -187,7 +196,7 @@ def can_use_rmsnorm_cast_before_weight(
         is_cuda()
         and device.type == "cuda"
         and dtype == torch.bfloat16
-        and eps == 1e-6
+        and eps in (1e-6, 1e-5)
         and contiguous
     )
 
@@ -232,7 +241,7 @@ def _valid_rmsnorm_cast_before_weight(
 
 
 def _fake_rmsnorm_cast_before_weight(
-    x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor
+    x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor, eps: float = 1e-6
 ) -> torch.Tensor:
     return torch.empty_like(x)
 
@@ -337,19 +346,22 @@ def rmsnorm_cast_before_weight_rope_bitexact(
     fake_impl=_fake_rmsnorm_cast_before_weight,
 )
 def rmsnorm_cast_before_weight_bitexact(
-    x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor
+    x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor, eps: float = 1e-6
 ) -> torch.Tensor:
-    """Match ``(x.float() * rsqrt(mean(x.float()**2) + 1e-6)).bf16() * w``."""
-    if not _valid_rmsnorm_cast_before_weight(x, weight):
-        raise ValueError("RMSNorm requires contiguous CUDA BF16 inputs and weight.")
+    """Match ``(x.float() * rsqrt(mean(x.float()**2) + eps)).bf16() * w``."""
+    if not _valid_rmsnorm_cast_before_weight(x, weight) or eps not in (1e-6, 1e-5):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "RMSNorm requires contiguous CUDA BF16 inputs and weight, "
+            "with eps=1e-6 or eps=1e-5."
+        )
     with torch.cuda.device(x.device):
         out = torch.empty_like(x)
         dim = x.shape[-1]
         rows = x.numel() // dim
         # At least 16 rows keeps ATen's reduction width at 32 lanes for
         # these dimensions. Smaller row counts can select a different tree.
         # Larger FP32 workspaces can make TensorIterator split the reduction.
-        if dim in (128, 3072) and rows >= 16 and x.numel() < 2**29:
+        if dim in (128, 3072, 3840) and rows >= 16 and x.numel() < 2**29:
             _ordered_norm_kernel[(triton.cdiv(rows, 4),)](
                 x,
                 weight,
@@ -358,6 +370,7 @@ def rmsnorm_cast_before_weight_bitexact(
                 dim,
                 4,
                 triton.next_power_of_2(dim),
+                eps,
                 num_warps=4,
                 enable_fp_fusion=False,
             )
@@ -367,6 +380,14 @@ def rmsnorm_cast_before_weight_bitexact(
         _square_kernel[grid](x, squared, x.numel(), 1024, enable_fp_fusion=False)
         mean = squared.mean(-1, keepdim=True)
         _normalize_kernel[grid](
-            x, mean, weight, out, x.numel(), x.shape[-1], 1024, enable_fp_fusion=False
+            x,
+            mean,
+            weight,
+            out,
+            x.numel(),
+            x.shape[-1],
+            1024,
+            eps,
+            enable_fp_fusion=False,
         )
     return out

@@ -8,7 +8,9 @@
 
 from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion import (
     BitExactFusionGate,
+    can_use_rmsnorm_cast_before_weight,
     fused_packed_silu_mul_bitexact,
+    rmsnorm_cast_before_weight_bitexact,
 )
 from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.distributed import get_sp_world_size
 from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.distributed.sp_shard_utils import (
@@ -26,6 +28,8 @@

<!-- amd-bot-suspect-fix:47118 -->
@BBuf AMD CI jobs started failing after this PR was merged, and #47118 proposes a fix. Could you review it?

test_ming_image.py::test_ming_norm_fusion_replay_and_native_fallback, added by this PR, is skipped only when torch.cuda.is_available() is false, which is never the case on ROCm, and it asserts that the fused RMSNorm kernel runs once. can_use_rmsnorm_cast_before_weight requires is_cuda(), so ROCm takes the native path and the test fails with call_count 0 on rocm10 and rocm724.

The last passing run was on [`586355a8`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/586355a83bdf609579b3309d4125620351156bb7) and the first failing run on [`9d2dae39`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/9d2dae3907e966caf483544dd699986d60846958); this PR's commit [`4b43572e`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/4b43572e522912641ca7c83c5045f8c92bdad4c4) is between them.

Failing jobs (2):
- [multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-amd (rocm10, linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang, 3)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40686510947/job/122810254546)
- …and 1 more

If this PR isn't the cause, please say so here so the attribution can be corrected.
